_comment: A four-slide interactive course presentation on the cardiac cycle. Slide backgrounds use placeholder images (as imported slides would); each slide carries positioned overlays — info hotspots that reveal text and checkpoint overlays whose inner configs are validated at render against the multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blanks schemas. The final slide is a blank summary divider.
title: The Cardiac Cycle
author: Kukui sample content

slides.title: What is the cardiac cycle?

background.alt: Title slide reading: Cardiac Cycle — Overview.

slides.notes: The cardiac cycle is the sequence of events in a single heartbeat: the alternating contraction (systole) and relaxation (diastole) of the heart's chambers. Explore the hotspot, then move on.

overlays.label: Systole vs diastole
overlays.html: Systole is contraction (ejecting blood); diastole is relaxation (refilling). The two alternate roughly 60–100 times a minute at rest.

background.alt: Slide illustrating the first and second heart sounds, S1 and S2.

config.title: The first heart sound (S1)
config.question: The first heart sound (“lub”) is produced primarily by the closure of which valves?

answers.feedback: Not quite — closure of the semilunar valves produces the second heart sound (S2), the “dub.”
Correct — S1 marks the start of ventricular systole as the AV valves snap shut.
Not quite — these valves close at different points in the cycle, so they do not produce a single combined sound.

background.alt: Slide showing the contraction and relaxation phases of the cardiac cycle.

config.title: Phases of the cycle
config.text: During *systole* the heart muscle contracts, while during *diastole* it relaxes and refills with blood.

slides.title: Summary
slides.notes: You stepped through the cardiac cycle: atrial and ventricular systole, then diastole, with valve closures producing the two heart sounds. Use the dots above to revisit any slide, then finish when you are ready.
